nodes.title: Owner presence by hardware key: approvals are OpenSSH signatures by the owner's touch-required key

contract.objective: An owner approval needs the owner's body, not a terminal. Today holden approve passes when standard input is a terminal and signs with a login-Keychain item that has no access control, so any agent in a terminal pane can approve. After this slice an approval is an OpenSSH signature in its own namespace (holden-approve) over the canonical approval payload, made by a hardware-held key that requires a touch, and verified against an allowed-signers file pinned in the private state. No software-held owner key can approve, and the terminal test is no longer the protection.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-embed/src/approve.rs, crates/holden-cognition/** (approval verification), crates/holden-cli/src/** (approve and owner-key commands, usage text), README, tests
acceptance_criterion: P1 in a disposable test install with throwaway keys only, an agent process running as the owner with a pseudo-terminal on standard input tries to approve and is refused; the test pins the exit code and the refusal text, and the refusal names the protection (no signature by the pinned touch-required key).

P2 verification accepts only sk-type keys (sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com, sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com) and checks the user-presence flag in the signature; mutants: drop the namespace check, accept a signature without the presence flag, accept a key that is not in the pinned allowed-signers file; each goes red.

P3 holden approve and owner-key setup never read or create a Keychain signing item; the stdin-terminal test is removed as a protection; earlier approvals stay verifiable and are reported as terminal-tested, not presence-proven.

P4 the approve usage and README name the protection and how to pin the owner's published signing key; a key type that cannot prove presence (for example a plain ecdsa key held by an agent app) is refused with a text that says why.
P5 tests never touch the owner's real Keychain, SSH agent, keys or private state; throwaway keys live in a temporary directory removed by a Drop guard.
P6 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

P7 no test in the workspace creates, changes or removes anything under the real private root: the gate snapshots the real root (names, types, link targets) before and after the suite and fails on any difference; mutant: a test that embeds without AGENT_PRIVATE_ROOT and the gate goes red. (Seen 2026-11-15: a dangling hosts/host symlink to a removed hm14-cli test temp dir, dated 2026-11-14 and probably made before the slice-17 server-run isolation fix (8c5568b), was found in the real root and quarantined.)

P8 one holden approve run needs exactly one signature, hence one key touch, however many cognitions it approves: the signed payload is the canonical manifest of every cognition id and promise digest in the run, and each cognition approval verifies by membership in a signed manifest; a test approves 50 cognitions with a throwaway sk key and counts one signing call; mutant: sign per cognition and the count test goes red.

acceptance_criterion: P1 a fixture charter host (INTENT, GUARANTEES, three DONE lists with numbered proofs, headings and prose) yields exactly its numbered proofs and guarantees as candidates, each with source path and line; headings, prose paragraphs and lines of 40 characters or less are not candidates; mutant: restore paragraph extraction and the test goes red on the count. nodes.title: One agent state belongs to one host, and a skipped holdout is never silent

contract.objective: The default agent state is keyed by the host folder name only, so two different repositories cloned under the same folder name share one state: its keys, its lens and later its approvals (wave 1: plangraph and odin both used hosts/holden-wave1-clone-20261115). After this slice a state records the host it belongs to (the canonical host path and the host repository root commit), a state is used only by that host, and every refusal text a host sees names paths relative to the host or to the private root, never an absolute home path. Also, a commit whose holdout did not run (holden not found by the hook, or the agent not serving) is recorded as not run, and the record is reported. And the number of cognitions an embed proposes is bounded: wave 0 on a large client proposed 9,869 cognitions (47 MB) for the owner to approve, more than anyone can read. The host files name the state by an opaque id, never by the host folder name, which can be a private or lane-specific name and would be committed with the host files.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-embed/src/** (state identity, refusal texts), crates/holden-cli/src/** (printing), README, tests, crates/holden-embed/src/host.rs (post-commit shim)
acceptance_criterion: P1 two fixture repositories with different root commits, cloned under the same folder name in two parent directories: the second embed is refused with a text that names the conflicting state as hosts/<name> and says how to proceed (a different folder name, or --state); the first host state is unchanged byte for byte; mutant: drop the identity check and the test goes red when the second embed succeeds.

P2 the same repository moved to a new path (same root commit) is refused with a text that says the state belongs to the old location, until the owner-documented re-home step is run; the step is in the README and tested.
P3 a state made before this slice (no identity recorded) is adopted by the first embed that uses it and recorded from then on; a test pins it.

P4 no refusal or report text from embed, jit, trace or agent serve contains the user home directory or an absolute path outside the host; a test runs each refusal with a sentinel home and scans the output.

P5 the post-commit shim finds holden on PATH, else at the install location recorded relative to the user home (never an absolute path in the host); when neither exists it prints one line naming the missed holdout and exits 0 without blocking the commit; a test runs it with an empty PATH.

P6 a jit that does not run a holdout (agent not serving, holden missing, no approved cognition) writes a not-run entry (commit, reason, time) to the agent state; W4 and holden trace list not-run commits beside the runs; mutant: drop the entry and the W4 count test goes red.
P7 the README states the minimum setup for one real holdout run on a host: embed, one owner approval, holden agent serve --host <host> in a visible pane (never a launchd job), then a commit.

P8 an embed proposes at most 50 cognitions by default, chosen deterministically and spread across the source documents (round robin by source, in file order); --max-cognitions <n> changes the bound; the report states how many candidates were not proposed and why; a host with 10,000 candidates writes at most 50 cognition files; mutant: drop the bound and the count test goes red.

P9 .holden/config.json and every other host file name the agent state as hosts/<id>, where <id> is derived from the host repository identity and a random value kept in the state; the host folder name appears in no host file; an existing hosts/<folder name> state is adopted and renamed on the next embed; a test embeds a host whose folder name is a sentinel string and scans every host file for it.
P10 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

nodes.title: Host sockets fit the platform limit

contract.objective: A host agent state puts its sockets at <state>/si and <state>/se. Under a real private root those paths are 112 to 117 bytes for the wave hosts, over the macOS sun_path limit of 104, so holden mcp exits with InvalidInput and /holden onboard cannot start on any wave host. The machine-level server already uses a short per-root directory under /tmp (distribution::socket_dir). After this slice every host socket lives in a short private directory derived from the state, and a path that would still be too long is refused with a text that says so. Tests also leave their temporary roots behind: one afternoon of real_repo runs left 66 GiB in the temporary directory, and 170 empty or dead holden-501-* socket directories had accumulated. And one real_repo run on the Mac started 56 cargo builds and 223 rustc processes at once (load 414, 36 GB swap on a shared machine).
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-embed/src/state.rs (socket paths), crates/holden-embed/src/distribution.rs (shared short-dir helper), crates/holden-mcp/src/** (bind and connect), README, tests, crates/*/tests/** (temporary roots), xtask/src/** (gate check)
acceptance_criterion: P1 a host whose state directory path is 200 bytes long serves both roles: holden mcp initializes and /holden onboard reaches holden_onboard; mutant: restore <state>/si and the test goes red with the platform error. The same holds for the user-scope holden MCP server registered once per user and started with the host as its working directory: a test starts it from a host with a 200-byte state path and completes initialize.

P2 the short socket directory is created 0700, owned by the user, refused if it exists with another owner or wider mode, and is unique per state and role (two states never share a socket); tests pin each refusal.
P3 a socket path over the platform limit is refused before bind with a text naming the limit and the length, never the bare InvalidInput; a test pins the text.
P4 existing hosts keep working after upgrade without re-embedding; a test upgrades a slice-18 state.

P5 every test that creates a temporary root or a socket directory removes it when it passes and when it fails (a Drop guard, never a glob); the gate lists the temporary directory entries before and after the suite and fails if any new holden or hm entry remains; mutant: drop the guard in real_repo and the gate goes red.

P6 the real_repo test and the gate bound their own parallelism: at most one fixture cargo build at a time, each with at most CARGO_BUILD_JOBS (default 4) jobs, whatever --test-threads is; a test counts the concurrent child cargo processes and fails above one.
P7 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

nodes.title: Command output a seat can act on

contract.objective: Wave 1 examiners found: a successful embed prints no next step, although the exact owner command (holden approve --host .) is written into .holden/promise-proposals.json; holden <command> --help prints the whole 76-line usage; bare holden says unknown command; holden ledger verify prints the ledger as an absolute path. After this slice each command says what to do next and prints no machine path. Client checks of slice 18b also found: an embed deletes stale cognition files from the host tree and prints nothing for them (1,184 files on one host), and a source document with no candidates (charter/INTENT.md, by design: it states goals, not numbered proofs) looks the same as a parse failure. A third client found numbered lines outside the proof list taken as promises: one DONE file lists its seven gate steps as a numbered list under Steps: before its Proofs: list.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-cli/src/** (usage, help and output), crates/holden-embed/src/embed.rs (the embed report only), crates/holden-cognition/src/adapters.rs (the charter planning adapter only), README, tests
acceptance_criterion: P1 a successful embed ends its stdout with the next steps: the exact owner command from promise-proposals.json, marked as the owner only, and the holden agent serve --host command; a test pins both lines and that they equal the file.
P2 holden <command> --help prints only that command usage and exits 0, for every command; bare holden prints the global usage and exits 2 with no unknown command line; tests pin each.
P3 holden ledger verify and holden ledger telemetry print the ledger as a path relative to the private root; a test with a sentinel home scans their output.

P4 every file an embed removes from the host tree prints one removed: <host-relative path> line, and the report ends with the count of files written, unchanged and removed; a test with a stale cognition pins the line and the count, and that nothing is removed without its line.

P5 a source document that yields no candidates is named in the report with the reason (for charter/INTENT.md: the intent card states goals, not numbered proofs; candidates come from DONE proofs and GUARANTEES); a test pins the line for a charter host.

P6 in a charter DONE list only the numbered lines of its proof list (the block that follows a line starting Proofs) are candidates; numbered lines under any other label or heading (Steps:, Gates, Out of scope) are not; a fixture DONE file with a numbered Steps: list before its Proofs: list pins it, and the slice-18b P1 fixture yields the same candidates as before.
P7 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

nodes.title: Proof lists under markdown headings

contract.objective: Slice 18e P6 took candidates only from the block after a line starting with the word Proofs. A client host labels its DONE proof lists with markdown headings instead (## Proofs 78 files, ## Fixed proof groups 77, ## Proofs (REV-4 ...) 14, ## Proof 1 — <title> 6), so its cognitions fell from 1,524 to 235 and 246 of 292 sources reported no candidates. The P6 wording was the plan author's error, not the DEV's. After this slice every common form of proof label is read, and gate steps are still excluded.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-cognition/src/adapters.rs (the charter planning adapter only), fixtures/clients/**, tests
acceptance_criterion: P1 a proof block starts at a line starting Proofs (as now) or at a markdown heading whose text contains the word proof or proofs, case-insensitive (## Proofs, ## Proofs (REV-4 ...), ## Fixed proof groups, ## Proof 1 — <title>); it ends at the next heading without that word or at a top-level non-list line; a fixture DONE file per form pins each, and each yields exactly its numbered proofs.

P2 inside a proof block, top-level bulleted items (- or *) are candidates as well as numbered ones; indented sub-items (Reopen:, Fail-without mutant:, Test:) are never candidates; a fixture pins both.

P3 the 18e decoys stay excluded: numbered lists under Steps:, Gates, Out of scope or any heading without the word proof are not candidates; the 18b and 18e fixtures yield the same candidates as before.
P4 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

nodes.title: A proof candidate is the whole item

contract.objective: The charter adapter reads one line at a time, so a numbered proof that wraps onto indented continuation lines becomes a candidate holding only its first line, and the owner would sign a truncated promise. Client DONE files wrap most proofs. After this slice a candidate holds the whole item text, and its source span covers it. A second client numbers follow-up proofs 4b. and 4c.; the adapter accepts only all-digit numbers, so 4b. ends the block and drops 4b, 4c and the proof 5 after them. A re-embed of the first client after 18f still gave 0 candidates for 91 of 290 DONE files. Of these, 42 have a proof label followed by a prose paragraph (Run in app/ ..., Reopen for all: ...), and the prose ends the block before the first item. The other 49 have no proof label at all: their numbered proofs sit directly under the title heading.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-cognition/src/adapters.rs (the charter planning adapter only), fixtures/clients/**, tests
acceptance_criterion: P1 a numbered or bulleted proof item that continues on indented lines is one candidate whose text is the item through its last continuation line, joined with single spaces, and whose start and end bytes cover that span; it stops before the next item, before an indented sub-item (a line whose text starts with - or * , such as - Reopen: or - Fail-without mutant:), and at a blank line; a fixture with a three-line item pins the text and the span.
P2 an item whose name is bold (1. **name.** text) keeps its markers as written and is a candidate; a fixture pins it.
P3 single-line items and the 18b, 18e and 18f fixtures yield the same candidates as before; candidate ids of single-line items do not change.

P4 an item marker is digits optionally followed by one lower-case letter (4., 4b., 12c.); a lettered item is a candidate and does not end the proof block, so a numbered item after it (5.) is a candidate too; a fixture with 4., 4b., 4c., 5. pins all four.

P5 a proof block opened by a heading ends only at the next heading of the same or a higher level whose text lacks the word proof; prose, code fences and tables inside it are not candidates and do not end it; a lower-level sub-heading inside it does not end it. A fixture with ## Proofs, an intro paragraph, a ### sub-heading and numbered items pins all items.

P6 a block opened by a plain label line (Proofs, Proofs:, Proofs (...)) may begin with prose, including a label that wraps onto the next line, before its first item; after its first item a top-level line that is not an item or a continuation ends it, so the 18e Steps: and Gates decoys stay excluded. A fixture pins both.

P7 a DONE file with no proof label anywhere takes as proofs the top-level numbered items under its title heading, before its first second-level heading; numbered items under any other heading (## Gates, ## Schedule, ## Landing) are not candidates. A fixture pins both.

P8 the client cross-check names the exact commit of each client clone it counted, and gives three numbers per client: adapter candidates, the independent count, and the cognitions the embed writes, explaining any difference between candidates and cognitions.
P9 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

nodes.title: Embed checks its proof counts against charter's

contract.objective: holden and charter each parse a host's charter/DONE lists with their own parser. Five client findings in a row (wrapped items, lettered numbers, prose after a label, unlabeled lists, bold names) were holden's parser reading fewer proofs than the list holds, and each was found by a person counting by hand. A second team asked for the count to be checked by machine. charter gains a read-only command, charter done-count --json, that prints for every charter/DONE/*.md the number of proofs its own parser finds (object with schema_version charter.done-count/1, charter_commit, and lists[]: slice, path relative to the repository root, proofs as an integer, proof_ids). After this slice an embed of a charter host compares, list by list, the number of proof items holden's adapter recognised with charter's number, says so in its report, and refuses to propose cognitions from a list the two tools count differently. A charter that is absent, older than the command, or prints something holden cannot read never makes the embed refuse: the report says the counts were not cross-checked and why. The charter build that carries done-count is the pinned commit f006adbed3b89f43be8f6c79e6d791a7865cc994 (the same build as c6c9843 before charter history was rewritten on 2026-11-17) (charter/PIN.toml); the stubs follow the shape that build prints.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-embed/src/** (a count cross-check module and its call in embed), crates/holden-cognition/src/adapters.rs (expose the per-list count of recognised proof items before the length filter; no change to which items are candidates), crates/holden-cli/src/** (report lines, exit code, usage text), README, fixtures/clients/** (stub charter executables as shell scripts and their JSON), tests
acceptance_criterion: P1 on a charter host, embed runs charter done-count --json once with the host as its root, finding charter by HOLDEN_CHARTER_BIN when set and otherwise on PATH, with a time limit of 30 seconds; it reads only schema_version, lists[].path and lists[].proofs and ignores unknown fields; a test with a stub charter pins the invocation and the parse.

P2 the number compared for each list is the number of proof items holden's adapter recognised in that file BEFORE the 40-character minimum removes short ones, so a list with short proofs does not look like a mismatch; the report states per list how many recognised items were too short to be candidates; a fixture with one short proof pins equal counts.

P3 when every list's count equals charter's, the report says so in one line naming the number of lists compared and charter's commit as printed in charter_commit, and embed continues unchanged; a test pins the line.

P4 when a list's counts differ, embed exits 1, writes no promise proposals and no cognition files, and prints one line per differing list with the list path, holden's number and charter's number, then one line saying the two parsers disagree and the owner should not approve from this embed; the candidate report file is still written so the difference can be inspected; a test with a stub charter that reports one more proof than the fixture holds pins the exit code, the lines and the absence of proposals.
P5 a list present in charter's output and absent from holden's sources, or the reverse, is reported as a difference by path and counts as a mismatch under P4; a test pins both directions.

P6 charter absent (not on PATH and HOLDEN_CHARTER_BIN unset or naming no file), charter exiting non-zero (the older build's unrecognized subcommand, exit 2), charter exceeding the time limit, output that is not JSON, or a schema_version holden does not know: embed does NOT refuse; it prints one line starting counts not cross-checked: followed by the reason, and continues to the same result as an embed without the check; one test per case pins the line and that the proposals are identical to a run with the check skipped.
P7 a host with no charter/ directory makes no call to charter at all; a test with a stub that fails if called pins it.
P8 no line printed by the check contains an absolute path or the user home directory; the charter binary is named as charter, never by its resolved path; a test with a sentinel home scans the output.

P9 the README says what the check compares, that a mismatch stops the embed and why, and that an absent or older charter only prints the not-cross-checked line; the usage text of holden embed names HOLDEN_CHARTER_BIN.
P10 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names; no test calls an installed charter, only the stub executables in fixtures.

nodes.title: Proofs whose head line is a short name, and lists the adapter skipped, are found or reported

contract.objective: A re-embed of the first client after 18g gives 1610 cognitions from 287 of 290 DONE sources, and four DONE files with real numbered proofs still give none. Read at that client commit, they show three causes. (a) Two files write each proof as a short name on the numbered line (1. D1: or 1. **Reproduces the stored verdict.**) and put the claim in indented sub-items; 18g rightly stops an item's text before its sub-items, so the text is shorter than the 40-character minimum and the proof is dropped. (b) One file has its numbered proofs under the title and, far below, a sub-heading whose text contains the word proof (evidence, not a proof); the word makes the file count as labeled, the labeled block holds no items, and the title list is never read. (c) One file has its numbered proofs under a second-level heading that does not contain the word proof; every item carries an indented reopened: line. In all three the embed says only that the source has no candidates, the same words it uses for a document that truly has none, so each gap was found by a person. After this slice the three shapes yield their proofs, and a DONE file that holds numbered top-level items of which none became a candidate says so by name and count. A second client re-embed found a fourth cause that the total hid: its count of 170 matched the independent count only because two errors cancelled, 5 name-only proofs missed (cause a) and 4 design bullets taken. (d) That file's title heading names a slice whose name contains the word proof, so the title opened a proof block and the top-level bullets under a plain Design line became candidates.
contract.resource_scope: crates/holden-cognition/src/adapters.rs (the charter planning adapter only), crates/holden-cli/src/** (the per-source report line only), fixtures/clients/**, tests
acceptance_criterion: P1 a proof item whose own text (before its first indented sub-item) is shorter than the 40-character minimum and which has at least one indented sub-item is a candidate; its text and span run from the item through the end of its first sub-item that does not start with Reopen, reopened, Fail-without, Mutant or Test (compared without case), or through its first sub-item when all of them do; a fixture with 1. D1: and three sub-items, and one with a bold short name, pins the text and the span.
P2 an item whose own text reaches the minimum is unchanged: same text, same span, same id as after 18g; the 18b, 18e, 18f and 18g fixture pins stay green without edits.
P3 a short item with no sub-item is still not a candidate, and the report counts it under too short (P6).

P4 when a file's labeled proof blocks (label lines and headings containing the word proof) yield no item at all, the adapter reads the file as unlabeled under the 18g title rule: top-level numbered items under the title heading before the first second-level heading; a fixture with title items and a later sub-heading containing the word proof and no items pins them. A file whose labeled block yields at least one item is unchanged.

P5 when a file still yields no item, a top-level numbered list outside code fences in which at least one item has an indented sub-line starting with reopened:, Reopen or Fail-without (compared without case) is a proof list wherever it sits; lists without such a line (Steps, Gates, Schedule, Landing) are still not; a fixture with both under second-level headings pins the proof list in and the decoys out.

P6 for every DONE source the report states the number of top-level numbered items seen outside code fences, the number taken as candidates, and the number left out by reason (too short, outside any proof list); a source with numbered items and no candidate is listed under its own heading numbered items found, none taken with its path and count, distinct from sources with no numbered items; a test pins the three wordings.

P6b the title heading (the first level-1 heading of a DONE file) never opens a proof block because of its words; a slice name containing the word proof does not make the lines under the title a proof block. A fixture whose title is # Done list — say-proof-integrity, followed by a plain Design line with four top-level bullets, then a Proofs label with five numbered items, yields exactly the five; the title rule of 18g for files with no label is unchanged.

P6c a cross-check that compares only totals is not accepted as evidence: every count comparison in the QA of this slice is per file, and the QA names each file where the adapter and the independent counter differ in either direction even when the totals agree.

P7 the cross-check of 18g P8 is repeated by the QA on the three client clones at named commits, and for the first client at the commit of this finding the four named files yield 5, 6, 6 and 4 candidates; the QA lists every DONE file where numbered items seen exceeds candidates taken, with the reason counts.
P8 macOS and Linux gates are green with identical test names.

fast_lane.reason: Holdout checkpoints gate later frontiers by design.

scheduling.executor: A/DROID-MISSION-1 (Factory Mission: orchestrator = TEAM PM, worker = DEV WORKER, validator = QA WORKER) runs every DEV and QA node as one mission, frontier by frontier, until HOLDOUT-HC5 or a stop rule fires
scheduling.holdout_examiner: A/HLDT-1 authors and runs HOLDOUT nodes; sealed material never enters the build pod's context
scheduling.control_plane: A/EXEC-PM merges accepted slices, writes qa-pins, pushes main, and answers escalations; owner-only nodes go to the owner
scheduling.heavy_suite_policy: one heavy suite at a time per repository; the Tart VM is shared and must be cleaned of scratch after each slice
scheduling.owner_gate: OWNER-APPROVE-DEMO is the only owner node; it blocks SLICE-07-QA (P4) and therefore HOLDOUT-HC1, never SLICE-08-DEV

required_conformance: Before dispatching a DEV node, the mission orchestrator writes charter/DONE/<slice>.md from that node's contract (proofs with reopen steps and fail-without mutants), commits it, and runs charter gate <slice> --dispatch. QA uses charter freeze, an independent validator seat of a model family different from the worker, a charter.receipt/1 receipt and charter gate --accept. Stop rules S1-S7 bind.
